title: The Real Avoidance Threshold T(d)
content:
```lean
noncomputable def lllThresholdReal (d : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  (1 / ((d : ℝ) + 1)) * ((d : ℝ) / ((d : ℝ) + 1)) ^ d
```

This is the symmetric Lovász Local Lemma threshold $T(d) = \frac{1}{d+1}\left(\frac{d}{d+1}\right)^d = \frac{d^d}{(d+1)^{d+1}}$, written over ℝ so it can be compared directly with the irrational sharp threshold $1/(e(d+1))$. The sibling entry `lovasz-local-lemma-oq-02` proves the rational version of $T(d)$ is the algebraically optimal probability the symmetric LLL tolerates at maximum dependency degree $d$.
mathContext: $T(d)$ is the maximum of $x \mapsto x(1-x)^d$, attained at $x^\star = 1/(d+1)$.

title: Key Lemma: (1 + 1/d)^d ≤ e Without the Limit
content:
The parent entry conjectured that connecting the LLL to the sharp constant $e$ would 'require formalizing $e = \lim (1+1/n)^n$'. It does not. The entire analytic content is one Mathlib inequality:

```lean
theorem one_add_inv_pow_le_exp_one {d : ℕ} (hd : 1 ≤ d) :
    (1 + 1 / (d : ℝ)) ^ d ≤ Real.exp 1 := by
  ...
  have h1 : (1 : ℝ) + 1 / d ≤ Real.exp (1 / d) := by
    have := Real.add_one_le_exp (1 / d); linarith
  have h2 : (1 + 1 / d) ^ d ≤ (Real.exp (1 / d)) ^ d := pow_le_pow_left₀ hb h1 d
  have h3 : (Real.exp (1 / d)) ^ d = Real.exp 1 := by
    rw [← Real.exp_nat_mul, mul_one_div, div_self hdne]
  rwa [h3] at h2
```

Apply $1 + x \le e^x$ at $x = 1/d$, raise to the $d$-th power (monotone, base nonneg), and collapse $(e^{1/d})^d = e^{d \cdot (1/d)} = e$. No sequences, no limits.

title: Reciprocal Form: 1/e ≤ (d/(d+1))^d
content:
Since $\frac{d}{d+1} = \frac{1}{1 + 1/d}$, the key lemma flips to a lower bound on the avoidance factor:

```lean
theorem inv_exp_one_le {d : ℕ} (hd : 1 ≤ d) :
    1 / Real.exp 1 ≤ ((d : ℝ) / ((d : ℝ) + 1)) ^ d
```

The proof rewrites $(d/(d+1))^d = 1/(1+1/d)^d$ and applies `one_div_le_one_div_of_le` to the key lemma. This is the precise inequality that places the sharp threshold below the algebraic one.

title: Headline: The Sharp Criterion Implies the Avoidance Threshold
content:
Multiplying the reciprocal bound by $1/(d+1)$ gives $1/(e(d+1)) \le T(d)$ (`sharp_le_lllThresholdReal`). Hence the sharp criterion reduces to the avoidance condition the gallery already discharges:

```lean
theorem sharp_criterion_implies_threshold {d : ℕ} (hd : 1 ≤ d) {p : ℝ}
    (_hp : 0 ≤ p) (hsharp : Real.exp 1 * p * ((d : ℝ) + 1) ≤ 1) :
    p ≤ lllThresholdReal d
```

From $e \cdot p \cdot (d+1) \le 1$ we get $p \le 1/(e(d+1)) \le T(d)$. So no new induction is needed: the sharp constant $e$ is justified purely by reduction to the optimal rational threshold.

title: Strict Improvement: e < 3 Beats the 1/3 Criterion
content:
Because $e < 3$ (`exp_one_lt_three`, from `Real.exp_one_lt_d9`), the loose criterion $p(d+1) \le 1/3$ implies the sharp $e p (d+1) \le 1$ (`third_implies_sharp`) — replacing $1/3$ by $1/e$ only enlarges the admissible set. The improvement is strict:

```lean
theorem exists_sharp_not_third {d : ℕ} (hd : 1 ≤ d) :
    ∃ p : ℝ, 0 ≤ p ∧ Real.exp 1 * p * ((d : ℝ) + 1) ≤ 1
      ∧ 1 / 3 < p * ((d : ℝ) + 1)
```

The witness $p = 1/(e(d+1))$ saturates the sharp criterion ($e p (d+1) = 1$) yet has $p(d+1) = 1/e > 1/3$, so it is certified by the sharp criterion but rejected by the gallery's $1/3$ form. The improvement window is $\tfrac{1}{3(d+1)} < p \le \tfrac{1}{e(d+1)}$.
mathContext: $1/3 < 1/e$ since $e < 3$; the sharp threshold is the larger one.

title: Capstone: The Sharp Symmetric LLL
content:
```lean
theorem sharp_symmetric_lll {d : ℕ} (hd : 1 ≤ d) {p : ℝ} (hp : 0 ≤ p)
    (hsharp : Real.exp 1 * p * ((d : ℝ) + 1) ≤ 1) (n : ℕ) :
    p ≤ lllThresholdReal d ∧ 0 < ((d : ℝ) / ((d : ℝ) + 1)) ^ n
```

The textbook statement, now formally tied to $e$: under the sharp criterion, $p$ meets the LLL threshold and the avoidance product $(d/(d+1))^n$ is strictly positive — the bad events can all be simultaneously avoided.
